rationale: Evidence: iteration 8 (mass 0.4, wheel_track 0.10, kp 5.5, kd 2.5, sensors at y=0.08, x=-0.06..0.06, sensor_size 0.016) is the best raced design at 690.5. Oval finishes 20/20 (2.41 s), s-bend 20/20 (2.79 s), slalom 0/20 (progress 0.52, 17 off-track, 3 timeouts). Iteration 9 narrowed wheel_track to 0.09 and scored 676, so the narrower track did not help and is reverted. Iteration 7 (kp 6.0 with sensor spread +/-0.08) collapsed the oval and s-bend, so that spread and kp change is rejected. Across iterations 5 to 8, slalom progress was best with lower kd: kd 2.0 gave slalom progress 0.50 versus 0.42 at kd 2.5 (iteration 5 vs 6), while kd 2.5 gave s-bend 20/20 versus 19/20. The slalom is failing by leaving the tape at sharp direction changes, and high kd may be slowing the response there. Change, kept to one lever: kd 2.5 to 2.2 on the iteration-8 design, with geometry otherwise unchanged (wheel_track back to 0.10, mass 0.4). Expected result: slalom progress rising toward 0.55 to 0.6, oval and s-bend completion held, and steering_oscillation rising only modestly from the 0.12 to 0.15 (oval) and 0.15 to 0.2 (s-bend) range. Hypotheses: H1, lower kd improves slalom progress at sharp turns, shown by slalom progress above 0.55 and off-track events falling. H2, lower kd lets s-bend oscillation rise, shown by s-bend steering_oscillation above 0.2 or s-bend finishes dropping below 20/20; if so, kd should return to 2.5. H3, if slalom progress is unchanged, the limit is authority or speed at the sharp turn, and base_speed on the slalom is the next lever. Next measurements: progress and completion_time (speed versus stability), max_error and line_loss_events (stability), steering_oscillation (damping), control_effort (gain cost), and noise_robustness (margin on held-back tracks).
